extracted.intended_audience: journalism researchers, newsroom editors, and PR professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalised criteria (from Lewis et al. 2008) for press releases to be picked up by thinned newsrooms — emphasising minimal editorial work, timing, wire compatibility, supplied validation, and ready-to-use assets. Useful for PR practitioners crafting releases intended for immediate republication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-publish
rubrics_metrics.description: A pickup-worthy release must require minimal sub-editor effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political-economy point: a thinned newsroom literally cannot rewrite — it republishes. Releases should be structured and written so that sub-editors can publish with very little modification.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-rewrite-needed prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an inverted-pyramid lead, AP-style attributions, and avoid marketing adjectives that a sub will have to strip.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Releases riddled with promotional language force rewriting and so are less picked up at the busy desks they target. Adopt neutral news prose and standard attribution conventions to survive the editing pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-laundering pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch the release so it can be rewritten by PA/AP into wire copy, extending reach to many outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rubric question is: is the release pegged so a wire desk will treat it as news? If it fits wire-desk needs, it reaches far more outlets via wire re-publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Output-pressure exploit (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Send the release timed to arrive before the desk's production deadlines (e.g., early morning for evening papers; mid-afternoon for morning papers; before broadcast slots for radio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because newsrooms operate under strict production cycles, releases arriving at the right moment exploit output pressure and are more likely to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-source sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both the announcement and an external-quote validator (e.g., a quoted independent expert or trade-body comment) within the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thinned newsrooms can rarely make second-source calls; releases that supply their own corroboration or independent comment are much more likely to be picked up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-supplied B-roll / visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Include ready-to-use photographs, video, or other broadcast-ready media assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because broadcast desks cannot dispatch crews, picture- and B-roll-ready releases convert at radically higher rates. Supplying high-quality, rights-cleared visuals increases pickup probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: No 'see attached' friction
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed critical materials (statistical tables, methods, image rights) directly in the release rather than as attachments or behind portals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attachments or links that require extra steps create friction in the editing pipeline and reduce the chance of republication. Make all necessary material immediately accessible and clearly usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural-asymmetry awareness (ethical framing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that churnalism rewards resource-rich PR over lower-resource but potentially newsworthy sources; ethically-minded releases should surface context rather than exploit newsroom resource gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lewis et al. argue churnalism's political-economic effects advantage well-resourced PR. An ethical release considers this structural asymmetry and aims to provide contextual information rather than merely exploiting the newsroom's need for ready copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pickup-worthiness implication: production-cost reduction over intrinsic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Pickup is driven more by how much a release reduces newsroom production cost than by intrinsic news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The political-economic frame predicts that the most picked-up releases are those that make republication faster than ignoring them. Craft releases to minimize the time and effort required for reuse if the goal is broad pickup.
